summary:
In August 2026 a mob beat a transgender couple, Aurora Rush and Shae Sanders, over restroom use at Cypress Black Bayou Park in Benton. Sanders, who has a pre-existing spinal injury, and Rush, who suffered a concussion and blood pooling, were both charged with disturbing the peace; the sheriff's office recorded no arrest of any attacker that day, and a plea deal had not been signed. Rush was denied hospital care and taken to a men's jail.

Rush was held in a men's facility and searched by a male guard even though her driver's licence carries a female marker. The marker on her licence did not determine her housing or her search procedure in custody.

In the same period the municipality of Benton voted one of the country's most severe anti-trans restroom ordinances.

Gender-marker changes on Louisiana documents require surgical proof. A driver's licence marker change requires a physician-signed statement confirming successful sex reassignment surgery; a new birth certificate requires a certified court order confirming surgical gender change, with proof of a diagnosis recorded as "transsexual or pseudo-hermaphrodite" and of anatomical change.

Louisiana's 1997 hate-crime statute provides penalty enhancements for offences motivated by sexual orientation or perceived sexual orientation but does not cover gender identity, so gender-identity bias crimes fall to federal prosecution under the Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act of October 2009.

Gender-affirming care for minors is banned: the Legislature overrode the governor's June 2023 veto in July 2023, and the ban on puberty blockers, hormones and surgery took effect on 1 January 2024.

Marriage is recognised in Louisiana after the 2015 invalidation of the state's 2004 constitutional ban on marriage and civil unions and its 1988 and 1999 Civil Code provisions; married couples hold full joint adoption and parental rights, following the 2014 Costanza v. Caldwell ruling that granted the state's first adoption by a same-sex couple.

The state's unenforceable sodomy statute remains on the books, carrying up to five years' imprisonment, a $2,000 fine and sex-offender registration; a repeal bill failed 66-27 in April 2014.

Louisiana has no state law prohibiting gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing or public accommodations. The Movement Advancement Project scores its gender-identity policy at -8.75 out of 25 and its overall policy at -8.75 out of 47 as of 12 October 2026, leaving federal employment-discrimination processes as the main recourse. New Orleans and Shreveport prohibit gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations; Alexandria, Baton Rouge, Lafayette, Lake Charles and Jefferson Parish extend protection only to public employees.
tangentialFactors:
Louisiana's sex-education statute prohibits classes from discussing male or female homosexual activity.

A 2017 amendment to the state's domestic-violence law removed opposite-sex language, so sentencing no longer differs by the sexes of the parties; it passed 54-42 in the House and 25-13 in the Senate and took effect on 1 August 2017.

Louisiana barred transgender girls from public-school sports in June 2022, with more than two-thirds support in both chambers; a 2021 bill passed the House 77-17 and the Senate 29-6 but was vetoed, and the override failed by two votes.
localsOnly:
Yella (Robert) Clark Jr., a 45-year-old Black transgender woman serving a life sentence at Angola, was killed on 2 April 2024 in a fight with several other inmates. The Human Rights Campaign records her death in its memorial to transgender people killed that year.

Executive orders barring sexual-orientation discrimination in state employment, issued in 1992, 2004 and 2016, all lapsed, expired or were struck down and upheld on appeal in March 2018, leaving no protection on that ground for state employees.

Transition-related surgery, puberty blockers and hormone therapy are excluded from health insurance and from state Medicaid coverage, so residents pay for care out of pocket.
outOfScopeNotes:
Two further bills related to the 2023 minors' care ban remained awaiting legislative action when the sources were compiled; their status is unresolved.

The Human Rights Campaign states that killings of transgender and gender-expansive people are systematically under- or mis-reported, so the number of such deaths in Louisiana is not reliably established.

The Benton plea deal had not been signed at the time of the August 2026 reporting; the outcome of the charges against Rush and Sanders is unresolved.

The sources describe a municipal restroom ordinance in Benton; they do not describe any statewide facilities statute, so the state-level position on restroom access is not established by them.
